card.grading: The repo's own test/configCases and statsCases (thousands of fixtures) are split into hidden bucket subsets, with built bundle output executed and checked. Extra generated module graphs are compared with a sealed reference build for pruned export sets. Fraction passed.

Band.why: Frontier agents can recall much of webpack's structure, and no dated evidence of partial success was found, so cap at 3.

Build.why: Medium cost: an offline node_modules build plus a heavy test harness; the probe result is missing.

Fit.why: CPU-only JS, but the offline dependency install and the large test suite must be prepared in advance.

Hor.why: Sustained multi-module work across parser hooks and optimisation passes fits an 8 h tier.

Multi.why: Many config categories give natural partial-credit buckets.

Nov.why: Top l0 neighbour is 0.304, above the 0.15 bar, though those are internal seeds; not on the CROWDED list.

Real.why: Released upstream tag v5.112.0 with the four named files confirmed.

Ref.why: The complete upstream MIT implementation at the same commit.

Seal.why: The repo's own tests and fixture assertions ship in /app, so the oracle is in reach. Exact mangled names also encode the reference's internals.

Surf.why: Hundreds of configCases and statsCases fixtures, but they are the visible repo tests, so the surface is nominally large and effectively known.

spike_plan.kill_if: The suite is non-deterministic across three runs, needs network, or the stub failures do not map to the four files.
spike_plan.pass_if: Unmodified suite passes deterministically on the chosen subsets; stubbed files produce clear, repeatable failures; the no-optimisation cheat fails the export-set checks.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone webpack at v5.112.0 and run yarn install to produce node_modules.

Run the unmodified test harness on test/configCases/inner-graph, test/configCases/mangle and test/configCases/side-effects, plus a sample of test/statsCases. Record pass counts over three runs to check determinism.

Copy the repo and replace the four target files (InnerGraphPlugin.js, InnerGraph.js, FlagDependencyUsagePlugin.js, MangleExportsPlugin.js) with stubs that do nothing. Rerun the same subsets and confirm that the failures are real and not harness noise.
Check the 'disable optimisation' cheat: with optimization.usedExports, innerGraph and mangleExports off, see which fixtures still pass, and confirm that stats or export-set comparisons catch it.
Confirm no webpack copy is present elsewhere in the image (global npm, caches) that the agent could read.
Measure the test wall time per bucket to check the 8 h tier is reachable.

v1.summary: The repo, release and the four named optimisation files are confirmed, but the four files total about 1,600 code lines, not 2500+. The hidden cases are the repo's own test fixtures, which would ship in /app, and exact mangled-name matching encodes the reference, so the seed fails sealing (K11) unless the test tree is withheld and grading moves to a sealed generated-graph set.
